title: Ivo and the Contact
premise: Ivo Marchetti, a quiet archivist in Lisbon, is approached by Beatrix Halloran, a disgraced hostage negotiator who insists he once saved her life — a debt he has no memory of. The 'favor' was actually engineered by his late father, a fixer whose final ledger holds proof that a sitting minister ordered a massacre and let negotiators like Beatrix take the fall. When the people who buried the massacre come for the ledger, Ivo must choose between surrendering the secret that would clear Beatrix's name and destroy his father's posthumous protection of their family, or trading it away to keep them both alive. In the end Ivo leaks only half the ledger — enough to topple the minister and free Beatrix from her failure, but not enough to save himself from exile.
about_author: Jude Almeida is the pen name of a former crisis-line counselor who spent six years listening to negotiations go wrong from the outside of the glass. They write thrillers about ordinary people handed impossible ledgers of debt.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A woman waits outside Lisbon's national archive at closing time: Beatrix Halloran, who thanks him for saving her life in Oporto four years ago. He has never been to Oporto. She leaves him a photograph showing his father standing beside her on that day. Emotional beat: uncanny intrusion into an orderly life.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Sorting his dead father's effects, Ivo finds a hidden compartment: coded notebooks his father called 'the ledger,' plus a letter instructing him to burn them unread. Instead he photographs one page. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion of the man he mourned.

chapters.title: One Failure Still on the Board
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix works unattributed cases for a private firm, haunted by the Oporto siege where three hostages died and her career was quietly amputated. Her handler warns her off Halloran family business. Emotional beat: professional numbness cracking under old guilt.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix explains the photograph: a stranger pulled her from the kill zone before the breach, then vanished. Facial recognition says it was Ivo's father, António — meaning António knew the attack was coming. Someone is now following Beatrix. Emotional beat: alliance formed out of mutual need.

chapters.title: The Man Who Counts Everything
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Deciphering the ledger with Beatrix, Ivo realizes his father was a broker of secrets — and the Oporto entry names a payment from someone inside the Interior Ministry. That night his apartment is searched, professionally. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as a trap.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix pulls strings to identify the searchers: contractors tied to Minister Duarte Sarmento's security detail. Her own firm reports her inquiry upward within hours. Emotional beat: the machinery she served turning against her.

chapters.title: The Safehouse Rule
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo and Beatrix go dark in a fisherman's cottage near Sesimbra, trading decoded pages for stories. A slow intimacy forms between two people trained not to trust. Emotional beat: love beginning against both their instincts.

chapters.title: Half a Name
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The ledger's Oporto entry yields a codename — CARRION — but the identifying page is missing, cut out years ago. Beatrix recognizes the cutting style as her old handler's. Emotional beat: betrayal reaching back further than imagined.

chapters.title: What the Dead Man Promised
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo finds a second letter: António deliberately withheld one page to protect Ivo, promising a dangerous man named Vidal that the full ledger would never surface. The debt is generational. Emotional beat: anger at a father who loved him in cipher.

chapters.title: Vidal Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Vidal's POV (brief) then Ivo's. Vidal, António's old counterpart, abducts Ivo briefly to deliver terms: hand over everything by Friday or Beatrix dies first. He returns Ivo alive as a show of good faith. Emotional beat: terror wearing a courteous face.

chapters.title: Negotiation, Unattributed
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix does what she does best: opens a channel with Vidal, buying time by offering a partial trade. She hides from Ivo how much she's risking. Emotional beat: duty reasserting itself over the growing love affair.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Following his father's last known route, Ivo traces the cut page to a retired priest who kept António's confidences. The page names CARRION: Sarmento himself, and documents the massacre order verbatim. Emotional beat: the secret worth killing for finally in hand.

chapters.title: Two Truths
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. With proof in reach, Beatrix faces her own fork: publish and be vindicated, or trade it for safety. She realizes Ivo intends to give it up to save her. Emotional beat: love against duty, stated aloud for the first time.

chapters.title: Friday
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The exchange is set at a shuttered customs house. Ivo prepares a forged ledger while keeping the real page sewn into his coat — deceiving even Beatrix. Emotional beat: becoming his father's son, and hating it.

chapters.title: Customs House
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The trade goes wrong: Sarmento's men, not Vidal's, run the site. Beatrix is taken; Ivo escapes with the real page because they wanted him to run. Emotional beat: the trap snapping shut.

chapters.title: Collateral
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Held in a black site, Beatrix negotiates for her life using only what she knows of Sarmento's paranoia, planting doubt between the minister and Vidal. Emotional beat: survival as a conversational art.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Hunted, Ivo weighs burning the page and fleeing — survival bought with Beatrix's death and the victims' erasure. He contacts a journalist instead and splits the evidence. Emotional beat: choosing consequence over safety.

chapters.title: CARRION
chapters.summary: Journalist interlude, then dual POV. The leak detonates: the massacre order runs on every front page. Sarmento moves to erase everyone connected, ordering the site hit. Emotional beat: victory indistinguishable from escalation.

chapters.title: What Vidal Wanted
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Vidal surfaces, revealing he never wanted the ledger destroyed — he wanted Sarmento destroyed, and used Ivo as the lever all along. He offers Ivo the location of the black site. Emotional beat: learning the whole game was played above him.

chapters.title: The Breach
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Ivo guides police and press to the site while Beatrix talks her captors into standing down as the world watches live. Shots are fired; Vidal takes a fatal one shielding the exit. Emotional beat: climax — every debt called at once.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Sarmento falls; Beatrix is publicly cleared and offered her old career back. She and Ivo meet where they first met, outside the archive. Emotional beat: tenderness after ruin, and the cost acknowledged.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo burns the remaining ledger pages, keeping only the photograph of his father beside Beatrix. He writes one final entry of his own — what he traded, what it cost — and closes the book. Emotional beat: inheritance answered, not repeated.
